prompts.text: Which sound in our neighbourhood tells you the day is beginning?
Couples sometimes develop their own sense of timing around mornings and evenings.
A power cut interrupts our planned night in. What would turn it into a pleasant memory?
Tell me about a rainy day we spent together which ended differently from how you expected.
Watch a storm from the window or go outside after the rain clears?
Making ordinary inconveniences easier for each other is a meaningful kind of teamwork.
What change to your morning routine made life noticeably easier?
One of us needs to leave before sunrise for a few weeks. How should we protect each other's sleep?
Describe a journey home when you were especially looking forward to seeing me.
An early weekend breakfast out or a slow morning at home?
Which public place nearby would you enjoy making a regular stop together?
Neighbourhoods feel different when people start recognising the faces around them.
We find a community event happening within walking distance. What would make you want to join?
Tell me about the first time you felt at home in a new neighbourhood.
Feeling settled somewhere often has more to do with daily habits than the address.
What's one thing you would like us to learn about the people who live around us?
Help with a local clean-up or volunteer for an event we both care about?
Our neighbours disagree over a shared space. How would you want us to contribute constructively?
Recall a stranger who made one of our outings more memorable through a small kindness.
Two people often notice completely different details during the same walk.
What do you notice first when you enter an unfamiliar place?
Explore a museum slowly or wander through a local market together?
A good date doesn't need an elaborate plan if both people feel free to be curious.
We have a few hours in a city neither of us knows. What would help us decide where to go?
Tell me about a shared outing which taught you something unexpected about my interests.
Which kind of public event leaves you feeling energised rather than drained?
Partners needn't enjoy every activity equally to appreciate taking turns choosing.
I want to attend an event you're unsure about. How should I invite you without making it an obligation?
A live performance on Friday night or an art exhibition on Sunday afternoon?
Which experience would you be happy for me to enjoy with friends rather than join me yourself?
Describe an occasion when you supported an interest of mine even though it wasn't your thing.
Occasional separate outings give a couple fresh things to talk about.
We each receive invitations on the same evening. What would make our decision fair?
Different social batteries needn't cause conflict when people explain them openly.
What's your favourite way to reconnect after we've spent a day doing separate things?
Send photos from our separate days or save all the stories for when we meet?
Recall a time when I introduced you to someone who became important in your life.
Your closest friend and I approach a problem very differently. How would you want me to handle the difference?
You should never have to choose between a healthy friendship and a healthy partnership.
What's a quality in one of your friends you wish more people appreciated?
Meeting the people someone loves often reveals a side of their personality you hadn't yet seen.
Tell me about the first person in your life who seemed to understand why we worked well together.
Plan a small gathering with our families or spend a day visiting each home separately?
We want to introduce two relatives who have contrasting personalities. What would help everyone feel at ease?
How do you prefer to prepare for a family visit when you know the conversations might be demanding?
Politeness is easier to sustain when people agree on reasonable limits in advance.
Describe an old family story you would want our household to keep telling.
Family stories change subtly depending on who tells them and who is listening.
A relative asks a personal question neither of us wants to answer. How should we respond?
Share family recipes with each other or collect old photographs and learn their stories?
Which relative has a mannerism you recognise in yourself?
Tell me about a moment when you realised you'd adopted a habit from someone who raised you.
Knowing where a habit came from helps people decide whether they want to keep it.
We find our approaches to celebrating birthdays differ because of our childhoods. What would feel balanced?
Two people might express gratitude through entirely different gestures.
When someone says thank you, what helps you sense they have understood your effort?
Receive a thoughtful favour or hear specific words of appreciation?
Describe a time we showed gratitude to each other in an unusual way.
One of us plans a surprise the other finds overwhelming. How should we talk about surprises in future?
Which kind of affectionate gesture feels appropriate to you in public settings?
Comfort with public affection varies even between people who care deeply about each other.
Asking for affection directly is healthier than testing whether someone notices hints.
Tell me about a goodbye between us which stayed with you longer than you expected.
Hold hands during a walk or sit close while listening to music?
One of us reaches for a hug while the other feels overstimulated. How would you like us to communicate?
What helps you feel physically comfortable and respected when you're tired?
Recall a reassuring moment when simply having company made an unfamiliar place easier.
A familiar voice makes practical challenges feel less isolating without solving them.
We're waiting together for important news. What kind of conversation would you want in the meantime?
Patience is easier to offer when both people are honest about what they need.
How would you want me to respond if your plans changed because of circumstances beyond your control?
Talk about uncertain possibilities now or wait until we have reliable information?
Tell me about a change of plan which later turned into something worthwhile.
A financial setback forces us to postpone a shared goal. Which parts of the goal would you want to preserve?
Postponing a plan tests how strongly people agree on the reason behind it.
What's one long-term priority you would defend even if the timeline changed?
Flexibility is a skill couples learn by practising with small decisions.
Describe a time we adapted quickly and discovered we worked better together than expected.
Create a fresh plan every quarter or make a long-term map with room for changes?
What would make a conversation about our next five years feel hopeful rather than pressured?
Our ideas about the pace of life begin to diverge. How should we find a workable rhythm?
Dreams become easier to share when neither person treats them as immediate commitments.
Tell me about a hope you once kept to yourself because it felt too ambitious.
Sharing a dream doesn't oblige the listener to turn it into a project.
Which part of your future are you most interested in learning about rather than controlling?
Visit a place from your childhood or show me somewhere you hope to live one day?
We make a list of places important to our individual histories. Where would you want to begin?
Describe somewhere we went together which unexpectedly felt meaningful to you.
Returning to the same place over several years gives people a record of how their lives changed.
What's an annual tradition you would enjoy creating without copying anyone else's?
Couples benefit from traditions which evolve as their circumstances change.
A tradition we love becomes difficult to maintain. How would you decide what matters most about it?
Repeat a favourite anniversary activity or try an unfamiliar one each year?
Tell me about a tradition you outgrew and how you felt when you stopped it.
What do you hope our closest friends notice about how we treat one another?
People often remember how a couple handled a difficult moment more clearly than their photographs.
Someone asks what makes our partnership work. Which everyday example would you offer?
The most useful relationship advice describes habits rather than presenting a perfect couple.
Share advice we've learnt with younger relatives or keep our lessons mostly between us?
Recall a question somebody asked about us which made you reflect on our relationship.
